identification: Crate of lamps: (1) green Coleman pressure lantern with red Coleman decal, wide globe, valve wheel on the fount (looks like a 220-series two-mantle, model and date stamp not legible); (2) dark green Coleman pressure lantern with chrome base label, modern 1980s-2000s two-mantle type (looks like a 288/290-series), low value; (3) Tilley-type kerosene pressure lamp, black hood, grey-painted fount, brass pump, wire cage, rusty (Tilley X246 / Bialaddin type, maker not legible); (4) about five antique carriage/coach lamps: one large brass lamp with an oval bevelled front lens, two square brass-framed bevelled-glass lamps with brass sockets and ribbed candle tubes, a black japanned buggy lamp with round lens and long socket, a brass-trimmed square lamp with brass socket tube; plus a black tin square lamp (cycle/rail style), a loose wooden handle and a Jackeroo lantern mantle packet. Dusty, rust and verdigris, untested.

viewing_check: Check fount stamps on both Colemans (model and month/year, e.g. 220E/F/J or 288, made in USA/Canada) and whether the globes are intact; check the pressure lamp for a Tilley/Bialaddin/Vapalux stamp under the fount; count the carriage lamps, look for any matching pair, intact bevelled glass and maker names (Lucas, Salsbury, JN&S).
